[[1, 2]] 
The available analyst consensus was **$2.618 billion**, about **$43 million (1.7%) above** the high end of management’s range and **2.7% above** its midpoint, implying the principal near-term revenue-execution risk was expectations above formal guidance. [[3, 2]]

tool_arguments.query: Equinix Q2 2026 revenue $2.625 billion year-over-year growth AI demand

events.content: Equinix Q2 2026 revenue $2.625 billion year-over-year growth AI demand

Equinix reported Q2 2026 revenue of **$2.625 billion** for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, up **16% year over year** on both a reported and normalized constant-currency basis. [[1]] 

The headline growth included both strong underlying demand and one-time xScale fees: recurring revenue was **$2.377 billion**, versus **$2.143 billion** a year earlier, while non-recurring revenue rose to **$248 million** from **$113 million**. [[1]] 

Thus, recurring revenue grew about **10.9% YoY**, indicating that most of the underlying growth remained robust even excluding the unusually large non-recurring contribution. [[1]] 

AI demand appears to be a meaningful operational driver rather than merely a narrative: annualized gross bookings increased **23% YoY**, backlog reached a record, and Equinix added a record **9,700 net interconnections** in the quarter. [[2]] 

Management said customer demand was broad-based and growing, and specifically positioned Equinix to serve enterprise networking, cloud, and AI-infrastructure requirements. [[2]] 

The key analytical caveat is that the **16%** total-revenue growth rate should not be treated as fully recurring, because the company explicitly attributed part of it to one-time xScale fees; the recurring-revenue trajectory and bookings/interconnection metrics are cleaner indicators of sustained AI-led demand. [[1]] [[2]]

events.content: Equinix Q2 2026 xScale leasing 134 MW AI demand

**Equinix’s Q2 2026 xScale leasing was a strong indicator of AI-led hyperscale demand, but the company did not disclose that all 134 MW was AI-specific.** Equinix closed **134 MW of xScale leases** in the quarter, including the Hampton transaction, and reported that the deal contributed approximately **$120 million of non-recurring fees**. [[1]] 

Management said that “the vast majority” of its largest Q2 deals were driven by AI workloads, while characterizing AI as an accelerant to its broader digitization, cloud, connectivity, and sovereignty demand. [[1]] Therefore, the sound interpretation is that the 134 MW leasing result was **materially AI-influenced rather than a disclosed 134-MW AI-only booking figure**. [[1]] 

The financial impact was visible in reported results: Q2 revenue was **$2.625 billion, up 16% year over year**, with the company explicitly attributing part of that growth to one-time xScale fees. [[2]] Excluding xScale leasing fees, Equinix said adjusted EBITDA margin still increased by roughly **150 basis points year over year**, suggesting the underlying retail/interconnection platform was also performing strongly. [[3]] 

For capacity and capital deployment, Equinix said a significant portion of capacity planned for delivery in the remainder of 2026 had already been committed through bookings and presales, while guiding to **$5–$6 billion** of capital expenditure excluding real-estate acquisitions and xScale. [[1]]

**Q1 2026 revenue:** Equinix reported revenue of **$2.444 billion** for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, up **10% year over year** as reported and **8%** on a normalized, constant-currency basis. [[1]]

**AI demand / leasing:** The company delivered **$378 million of annualized gross bookings** and roughly **$140 million of annualized presales**—a record presales level—with approximately **60% of its largest deals AI-related**. [[1]]

**xScale timing:** Q1 revenue and results **did not include the Hampton xScale lease transaction**; Equinix said that, excluding the timing effect of that deal, Q1 performance was above the midpoint of its Q1 revenue-guidance range. [[1]]

**Read-through:** The deferred xScale lease is a timing issue rather than evidence of weak underlying demand, as management indicated it was negotiating expanded mutually beneficial terms and expected the associated economics to be reflected in Q2 guidance. [[2]]

**Important nuance:** Equinix did not disclose a stand-alone dollar amount for “AI leasing” revenue in Q1; the clearest disclosed AI indicators are the AI mix of large deals, the record bookings/presales, and the postponed Hampton xScale transaction. [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: Equinix FY 2025 full year revenue and AI xScale leasing

events.content: Equinix FY 2025 full year revenue and AI xScale leasing

Equinix generated FY2025 revenue of **$9.217 billion**, up **5% year over year as reported** and **6% on a normalized, constant-currency basis**, for the year ended December 31, 2025. [[1]] 

Its xScale hyperscale/AI platform had **more than 430 MW leased** across **23 operational facilities in 13 metros** at Q4 2025; Equinix also delivered **more than 90 MW of xScale capacity during 2025**. [[2]] [[3]] 

The reported xScale leasing figure is platform-wide leased power capacity rather than a separately disclosed FY2025 AI-only leasing subtotal. [[2]] [[4]]

Related coverage:
**Equinix (EQIX) dividend:** the current quarterly common-stock dividend is **$5.16 per share**, a 10% increase, payable March 18, 2026 to shareholders of record February 25, 2026. [[1]] 
Annualizing that rate implies **$20.64 per share**, subject to future board declarations. [[1]] 

For comparison, Equinix distributed **$4.69 per share per quarter**, or **$18.76 annualized**, during 2025. [[2]]

**REIT payout:** a REIT must distribute at least **90% of REIT taxable income**—calculated before the dividends-paid deduction and excluding net capital gains—to preserve REIT qualification; this is a tax-income test, not an AFFO payout-ratio target. [[3]] [[4]] 

Using Equinix’s 2026 guidance, expected cash dividends of approximately **$2.036 billion** represent about **48.0%–49.0% of guided AFFO** of $4.158–$4.238 billion; on a per-share basis, the $20.64 annualized dividend is about **48.3%–49.2%** of guided diluted AFFO per share of $41.93–$42.74. [[5]] 

Thus, Equinix’s cash dividend is roughly a **48%–49% AFFO payout**, while its legally required REIT distribution percentage is measured against taxable income and is at least 90%. [[5]] [[3]]

private_messages.content:
Equinix reported Q2 2026 revenue of **$2.625 billion** for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, up **16% year over year** on both a reported and normalized constant-currency basis. [[1]] 

The headline growth included both strong underlying demand and one-time xScale fees: recurring revenue was **$2.377 billion**, versus **$2.143 billion** a year earlier, while non-recurring revenue rose to **$248 million** from **$113 million**. [[1]] 

Thus, recurring revenue grew about **10.9% YoY**, indicating that most of the underlying growth remained robust even excluding the unusually large non-recurring contribution. [[1]] 

AI demand appears to be a meaningful operational driver rather than merely a narrative: annualized gross bookings increased **23% YoY**, backlog reached a record, and Equinix added a record **9,700 net interconnections** in the quarter. [[2]] 

Management said customer demand was broad-based and growing, and specifically positioned Equinix to serve enterprise networking, cloud, and AI-infrastructure requirements. [[2]] 

The key analytical caveat is that the **16%** total-revenue growth rate should not be treated as fully recurring, because the company explicitly attributed part of it to one-time xScale fees; the recurring-revenue trajectory and bookings/interconnection metrics are cleaner indicators of sustained AI-led demand. [[1]] [[2]]

private_messages.content:
Equinix generated FY2025 revenue of **$9.217 billion**, up **5% year over year as reported** and **6% on a normalized, constant-currency basis**, for the year ended December 31, 2025. [[1]] 

Its xScale hyperscale/AI platform had **more than 430 MW leased** across **23 operational facilities in 13 metros** at Q4 2025; Equinix also delivered **more than 90 MW of xScale capacity during 2025**. [[2]] [[3]] 

The reported xScale leasing figure is platform-wide leased power capacity rather than a separately disclosed FY2025 AI-only leasing subtotal. [[2]] [[4]]

Related coverage:
**Equinix (EQIX) dividend:** the current quarterly common-stock dividend is **$5.16 per share**, a 10% increase, payable March 18, 2026 to shareholders of record February 25, 2026. [[1]] 
Annualizing that rate implies **$20.64 per share**, subject to future board declarations. [[1]] 

For comparison, Equinix distributed **$4.69 per share per quarter**, or **$18.76 annualized**, during 2025. [[2]]

**REIT payout:** a REIT must distribute at least **90% of REIT taxable income**—calculated before the dividends-paid deduction and excluding net capital gains—to preserve REIT qualification; this is a tax-income test, not an AFFO payout-ratio target. [[3]] [[4]] 

Using Equinix’s 2026 guidance, expected cash dividends of approximately **$2.036 billion** represent about **48.0%–49.0% of guided AFFO** of $4.158–$4.238 billion; on a per-share basis, the $20.64 annualized dividend is about **48.3%–49.2%** of guided diluted AFFO per share of $41.93–$42.74. [[5]] 

Thus, Equinix’s cash dividend is roughly a **48%–49% AFFO payout**, while its legally required REIT distribution percentage is measured against taxable income and is at least 90%. [[5]] [[3]]
